evidence.claim: A mountain parks road climbs from spruce forests into alpine country
evidence.quote: up through deep spruce forests and into the magnificent splendor of the alpine environment.

evidence.claim: The Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway climbs more than 7,000 feet in 28 miles, leaving forest for country above timberline.
evidence.quote: The Mount Blue Sky (formerly Mount Evans) Scenic Byway climbs more than 7,000 feet in just 28 miles

evidence.claim: On the upper road, steep grades, narrow pavement and winding turns shape the drive.
evidence.quote: steep, narrow, winding road

evidence.claim: The full 49-mile corridor is a Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway and a National Forest Scenic Byway.
evidence.quote: a 49-mile (79 km) National Forest Scenic Byway and Colorado Scenic and Historic Byway

evidence.claim: CDOT highlights its alpine lakes, wildflowers and Front Range views, and gives a driving time of two hours.
evidence.quote: Driving time: 2 hours

evidence.claim: Denver Mountain Parks planned the road to connect Echo Lake and Summit Lake with its lower foothill parks.
evidence.quote: The road was originally planned by the Denver Mountain Parks system to link Summit Lake Park and Echo Lake Park to their lower altitude parks in the foothills.

evidence.claim: Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. set the route, with scenic views part of the plan from the beginning.
evidence.quote: From the start, the road was planned in terms of the scenic vistas along the way.  The route was set by Frederick Law Olmsted Jr.

evidence.claim: Construction reached Echo Lake in 1921; the final 600 feet of the summit road were built by hand and completed in 1930.
evidence.quote: the last 600 feet (180 m) were finally built by hand, being completed in 1930.

evidence.claim: From Idaho Springs, follow Highway 103 to Echo Lake, then Highway 5 toward the summit.
evidence.quote: State Highway 103 from Idaho Springs, Colorado on I-70 about 13 miles (21 km) to Echo Lake, and Colorado 5 from Echo Lake 15 miles (24 km)

evidence.claim: The climb passes Mount Goliath and Summit Lake before ending at a parking area just below the peak.
evidence.quote: The byway visits Echo Lake Park, the Mount Goliath Natural Area, the Dos Chappell Nature Center, and Summit Lake Park on its way to the summit.

evidence.claim: The wider corridor also extends east from Echo Lake to Bergen Park on Clear Creek County Road 103 and Jefferson County Road 66.
evidence.quote: The eastern portion of the byway travels from Echo Lake to Bergen Park via Clear Creek County Road 103 and Jefferson County Road 66.

evidence.claim: The Mount Blue Sky Scenic Byway climbs more than 7,000 feet in 28 miles, leaving forest for country above timberline.
evidence.quote: brings you to the rarefied world above timberline

evidence.claim: CDOT highlights its alpine lakes, wildflowers and Front Range views
evidence.quote: the entire Front Range sprawls at your feet

evidence.claim: CDOT highlights its alpine lakes, wildflowers and Front Range views
evidence.quote: hardy wildflowers, lichens and grasses, furry mammals like pikas and marmots, rock-jumping mountain goats, and alpine lakes.

evidence.claim: Construction reached Echo Lake in 1921
evidence.quote: By October 1, 1921, the Bureau of Public Roads had completed construction to Echo Lake.

evidence.claim: ending at a parking area just below the peak
evidence.quote: ending at a parking area and turnaround just below the summit.

evidence.claim: Echo Lake owes its basin to retreating ice: glacial moraines blocked drainage in the Chicago Creek valley and formed a natural dam.
evidence.quote: As glaciers retreated in the Chicago Creek valley, lateral moraines formed a natural dam to drainage, forming the lake.

evidence.claim: The shallow lake lies at 10,600 feet, among Engelmann spruce and subalpine fir.
evidence.quote: Echo Lake is a shallow, oligotrophic lake situated at 10,600 ft

evidence.claim: Its park belongs to the Denver Mountain Parks system.
evidence.quote: The park is part of the Denver Mountain Parks system.

evidence.claim: At one end is a stone picnic shelter; at the other is Echo Lake Lodge, built in 1926.
evidence.quote: The park provides a stone shelter with picnic tables and barbecue grills on one end of the lake, and the 1926 Echo Lake Lodge

evidence.claim: Architect Jacques Benedict gave the lodge two octagonal log stories on a base of local granite.
evidence.quote: designed by Denver architect Jacques Benedict, a two-story octagonal log building on a base of local granite

evidence.claim: among Engelmann spruce and subalpine fir
evidence.quote: The ecosystem around the lake is dominated by Engelmann Spruce (Picea engelmannii) and Subalpine Fir (Abies lasiocarpa)

evidence.claim: Summit Lake sits in a glacial cirque on the north face of Mount Blue Sky and the east face of Mount Spalding.
evidence.quote: Summit Lake is a tarn which sits at 12,836 feet (3,912 m) elevation in a glacial cirque on the north face of Mount Blue Sky and the east face of Mount Spalding.

evidence.claim: At 12,836 feet, this lake is the headwaters of Bear Creek.
evidence.quote: The park is named after Summit Lake, the headwaters of Bear Creek.

evidence.claim: Permafrost east of the water helps prevent drainage, and the park contains alpine tundra.
evidence.quote: contains alpine tundra. Land to the east of the lake is in a state of permafrost which helps to prevent drainage of the area.

evidence.claim: Denver acquired the land in 1924 and brought it into the Mountain Parks system.
evidence.quote: The land was acquired by Denver in 1924 and incorporated into the Denver Mountain Parks system.

evidence.claim: In April 1965, it became a National Natural Landmark.
evidence.quote: It was declared a National Natural Landmark in April 1965.

evidence.claim: At 12,836 feet
evidence.quote: sits at 12,836 feet

evidence.claim: The summit road gave researchers access to high-altitude experiments as well as mountain views.
evidence.quote: The easy access to the summit provided by the Mount Blue Sky Highway has made it a popular location for scientific research.

evidence.claim: Arthur H. Compton studied cosmic rays here in 1931, shortly after the road was completed.
evidence.quote: Arthur H. Compton conducted pioneering research on cosmic rays on the mountain in 1931, shortly after the road to the summit was completed.

evidence.claim: The University of Denver built two A-frame buildings to house researchers.
evidence.quote: The University of Denver built a pair of A-frame buildings on the summit to house cosmic-ray researchers.

evidence.claim: Another summit structure met a different end: Crest House burned in 1979 and was never rebuilt.
evidence.quote: it burned down on September 1, 1979, and was not rebuilt

evidence.claim: Its rock foundation and walls remain, serving as a windbreak for mountain travelers.
evidence.quote: The rock foundation and walls remain as a windbreak for mountain travelers

evidence.claim: The summit road is seasonal. CDOT lists Memorial Day through Labor Day for summit access and requires vehicle reservations.
evidence.quote: Summit open Memorial Day through Labor Day only

evidence.claim: requires vehicle reservations
evidence.quote: Reservations are required for vehicle entry at Mount Blue Sky.

evidence.claim: The original plan approached Echo Lake from Bergen Park before climbing to the summit; the road down Chicago Creek Canyon was a secondary branch.
evidence.quote: As originally planned, the road ran from Bergen Park near Evergreen to Echo Lake, and then to the summit, while the road from Echo Lake down into Chicago Creek Canyon was a secondary branch.

evidence.claim: Outside the lodge, a historic plaque commemorates cosmic-ray experiments conducted at the lake and on the mountain between 1935 and 1960.
evidence.quote: in honor of many cosmic-ray physics experiments conducted at the lake and on the mountain between 1935 and 1960.  The historic plaque is outside the Echo Lake Lodge.

evidence.claim: North of the lake, a saddle looks down toward the two cirques holding the Chicago Lakes, at the headwaters of a different stream, Chicago Creek.
evidence.quote: To the north, there is a col (12,855 feet/3918 m elevation) looking down into the chain of two cirques holding the Chicago Lakes at the headwaters of Chicago Creek.

evidence.claim: In 1939, Bruno Rossi used sites at Mount Blue Sky, Echo Lake, Denver and Chicago to measure the lifetime of the muon.
evidence.quote: The first accurate measurement of the lifetime of the muon (originally called the mesotron) by Bruno Rossi in 1939, used sites at Mount Blue Sky, Echo Lake, Denver and Chicago.

evidence.claim: A mountain parks road
evidence.quote: The road was originally planned by the Denver Mountain Parks system
